clue.text: Pick up lock key then lay down

indicators.note: to pick something up is to lift it, and lifting the letters turns them back to front in this reading

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Instructions for a burglar or locksmith: pick the lock, use a key, then put it down.
explanation.walkthrough: TRESS then A, picked up, reads ASSERT. 'Lay down' is meant in the sense of laying down the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to state it firmly, as when one lays down a rule or principle.

clue.text: Roman Io stirred Cupid

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman is aroused by Io, the maiden loved by Jupiter, so Cupid has been at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is the nymph from classical myth whom Jupiter seduced, which fits the Roman scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An amorino is a small chubby winged figure in art, a putto representing the god of love.

clue.text: See 27

blocks.note: surface reading: a pointer sending the solver to another clue
setter's reading: this light holds the last word of the name clued at 27 across

explanation.definitionFit: The clue at 27 across defines a former South African province, and this light completes its three-word name.

clue.text: All lit up in rave to raise charity

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising letters means writing them from bottom to top, so they read backwards
one piece is placed in the middle of the other

blocks.note: to rave is to rant
aid given to those in need is charity

explanation.surface: A charity fundraiser held at a rave, with everyone lit up and glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All lit up' suggests a drunk raver, but here it means shining; in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means glowing or shining brightly, which is what something lit up all over does.

clue.text: Covert introduction of Scripture to cult

indicators.note: something introduced into a group goes inside it, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject once called Scripture
a sect is a cult or breakaway religious group

explanation.surface: A cult covertly bringing new recruits into its own version of Scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools RE (religious education) used to be called Scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covert is hidden from view, kept quiet and not openly revealed, which is what secret means.

clue.text: Strangely overlooked old solvers smuggling currency

indicators.note: smugglers hide goods inside something else, so one piece is carried inside the other
read as looked over, as in turned over, the whole construction is flipped end to end in this down answer

blocks.note: solvers are addressed as you, and ye is the old form of that word
lire are units of Italy's currency, replaced by the euro in 2002

explanation.surface: A tale of forgotten veteran crossword solvers caught running contraband money, oddly unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: YE holds LIRE to make YLIREE, which turned over reads EERILY. 'Overlooked' looks like 'ignored' but signals the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerily is an adverb meaning in a weird, uncanny or unsettling manner, close to strangely.

clue.text: Commentary about the mother of two monarchs

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
ma is a homely word for mother
the first monarch is R, for rex or regina, the second is KING written out

explanation.surface: Commentary on a royal mother who bore two monarchs, like a TV report on the Queen Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Mother was mother to Elizabeth II; here the two monarchs give R and KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarking is the act of passing comments on something, so it can stand for a running commentary.

clue.text: Au fait with top Newcastle United form?

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
putting letters into a new form rearranges them

blocks.note: the first letter of the city's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan who keeps up with how Newcastle United are playing at the top of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle United is an English Premier League football club, so 'form' reads naturally as its results.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tuned in to something means being alert and well informed about it, which is au fait with.

clue.text: Tony Short added fungi raised on the farm as part of the bill

indicators.note: a short name is missing its last letter
in a down answer, raising letters means writing them upwards, so they read backwards

blocks.note: Tony Blair, then Prime Minister, with his surname's last letter dropped
ceps are edible mushrooms
a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, briefly, adding mushrooms grown on the farm to the restaurant bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bill' is British slang for the police; Special Branch is the police unit for national security. Tony was then Prime Minister Blair; 'on' puts the farm below the raised pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Special Branch is a department of British police forces, so it is one division of the Old Bill.

clue.text: Lisa is keener, they say

definitions.note: the name that comes before Lisa in Leonardo's portrait title

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound of a word is what counts

blocks.note: a keener wails over the dead, a moaner; in a non-rhotic accent the two sound alike

explanation.surface: A claim that Lisa is the more eager of two people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keener' looks like an adjective, more eager, but it is the noun for a mourner who wails.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's portrait, so Lisa calls up her partner word Mona.

clue.text: Division intended to report after leave

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is wanted for its sound

blocks.note: to leave is to depart
intended means meant, which sounds like this word ending

explanation.surface: Someone meant to file a report before going on leave from their division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the sound-alike piece behind DEPART; the surface makes leave a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a section or division of a larger organisation such as a firm or government.

clue.text: Flicks off hospital machine switch

indicators.note: turning something off removes it, so a letter is taken out
to switch things round is to change their order

blocks.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flicks the switch to turn off a hospital machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flicks' looks like a verb but is the old slang noun for films; MACHINE loses its H and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The flicks is informal for the cinema, from the flickering image of early films.

clue.text: 2 type of beetle

definitions.note: 2 refers to the answer at 2, which is STATE

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the states of the USA
second meaning: a striped pest of potato crops

explanation.walkthrough: The bare number points to the answer at 2-down, which is STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is a western American state, and the Colorado beetle is a notorious potato-eating pest.

clue.text: The pledge of confinement

blocks.note: first meaning: the act of committing oneself to something
second meaning: sending someone to prison or a hospital

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, like a promise made by a prisoner, but splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Committal covers both binding oneself by promise and the legal act of committing someone to custody or an institution.

clue.text: Depressed spirit sinks off without energy into the gloom

indicators.note: pushed down the other way, the letters read upward in this down answer
off means gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled
without here means outside, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: rum is a spirit
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A depressed person's mood sinks, lacking energy, into gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface sounds like low spirits, but 'spirit' is a drink and 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Murkiness is darkness and dimness, the condition of being gloomy and hard to see through.

clue.text: The last charge to Jerusalem

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A final military charge on Jerusalem, as in a crusade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last charge' reads as one battle, but it splits into the alphabet's last letter and a charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: Zion is the hill on which Jerusalem stands, and its name is used for the city itself.

clue.text: Middlebrows regret backing common currency

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter
going backwards, the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the central letter of the five-letter word, once the clue's first word is split as middle plus brows
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Middlebrow types regret backing the single European currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middlebrows' must be split into middle and brows. The euro was the shared currency of the European Union, launched as notes and coins in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the single money shared by many European Union countries, hence common currency.

clue.text: Given new powers, penal centre became sanguinary

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: the three middle letters of the word
sanguinary means bloody, so to become so is to bleed

explanation.surface: A prison, given new powers, became a bloody place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanguinary' usually means bloodthirsty, but here it is just covered in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enabled is to be given the power or means to do something one could not before.

clue.text: They'll make short work of things

definitions.text: They'll make short work of things

blocks.clueFragment: They'll make short work of things
blocks.note: surface reading: people who finish jobs quickly
setter's reading: people who literally make texts shorter, editors who cut them down

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for doing something fast is taken literally, as shortening written works.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridger shortens a book or text by cutting it, so they produce short versions of works.

clue.text: Endlessly abuse a right to be withdrawn

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: abuse is insult, minus its final letter
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps on abusing a right will end up being taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' looks like taken back, a right withdrawn, but it means reserved in character.
explanation.definitionFit: An insular person is inward-looking and cut off from others, as an island is, so withdrawn.

clue.text: Flush out Peter, the French prisoner

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the name's letters are rearranged
a prisoner is held inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Peter flushes out a French prisoner hiding somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flush out' reads as a single verb, but 'Flush' is the definition and 'out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be flush is to be full or well supplied, as replete means filled or well stocked.

clue.text: For example, lead and drive high up, finding top gear

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: lead is one example of a metal mined as ore
to lob is to hit a ball high

explanation.surface: Golf or tennis talk: leading and hitting high shots puts a player in top gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' sounds like a car's highest gear, but it is clothing worn on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket worn over the upper body, so it is a garment for the top half.

clue.text: Absurd ambition, not one to end in a province

indicators.note: not having one means a letter standing for one is taken away
something absurd is nonsensical, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
the letter A from the clue is put at the end

explanation.surface: An absurd ambition, not one that will end in a province.
explanation.walkthrough: One I comes out of AMBITION, the remainder is rearranged, and A is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the ten provinces of Canada, in the middle of the country.

clue.text: Washington Irving's hollow shelter bagged by mole

definitions.note: the adjective in the title of his tale of the headless horseman

indicators.note: something bagged is put inside a bag, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side
a mole is a spy working inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A mole hides in a hollow, an animal's shelter as in an American tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the burrowing animal, but it is an undercover agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington Irving wrote The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, so the hollow he made famous is the sleepy one.

clue.text: Dainty morsel of mackerel, finely sliced

indicators.note: a morsel is a small piece, so the answer is a small part of the following words
sliced across the words, a run of letters is cut out of them

blocks.note: found inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A dainty piece of mackerel, thinly sliced, as on a plate of sashimi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finely sliced' adds to the cooking scene but also hints the answer is cut from the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicately built, like an elf, which is to say dainty.

clue.text: Cut out the occasionally Prussian style of skirt

blocks.note: blue is a colour that is sometimes Prussian, as in Prussian blue
a pencil skirt is a narrow straight style

explanation.surface: A dressmaker cutting out a skirt in a Prussian style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' sounds like a dressmaking verb, but it is the editor's act of deleting text. Prussian blue is a deep blue pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil a text is to censor or delete parts of it, from the colour editors used to mark cuts.

clue.text: See 27

blocks.note: surface reading: a pointer sending the solver to another clue
setter's reading: this light holds the middle word of the name clued at 27 across

explanation.definitionFit: The clue at 27 across defines a former South African province, and this light holds the middle part of its three-word name.

clue.text: He has the power to cut blades - grass?

definitions.text: He has the power to cut blades - grass?

blocks.clueFragment: He has the power to cut blades - grass?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone with a powered mower cutting blades of grass
setter's reading: an absolute ruler who holds all power, and can cut down anyone, even an informer, or grass

explanation.walkthrough: The mower image misleads: a grass is British slang for an informer, the kind a tyrant has dealt with, and the word ends in grass's slang sense, pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant who rules with absolute power and can have opponents removed at will.

clue.text: (and 25, 2) The once fruitless condition re-called by Nelson?

definitions.text: The once fruitless condition re-called by Nelson?

blocks.note: surface reading: a former barren state; setter's reading: a former name meaning a state free of a fruit
setter's reading: renamed under Nelson Mandela's government, which dropped the fruit from the name

explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer runs across 27, 25 and 2. 'Re-called' means given a new name, not summoned again: the province dropped the fruit in 1995 under President Nelson Mandela.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Free State was a Boer republic and later a South African province, renamed simply Free State after apartheid ended.
